study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Segal et al., Biological Psychiatry: Cognitive Neuroscience and Neuroimaging, 2025
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Multiscale Heterogeneity of White Matter Morphometry in Psychiatric Disorders

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study employed warped Bayesian linear regression (WBLR) normative models to map interindividual variability. The models were implemented using the PCNtoolkit (version 0.21).
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Segal2025.pdf.md: ABSTRACT / METHODS; Segal2025.pdf.md: METHODS AND MATERIALS / Voxel-Scale WMV Heterogeneity
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: We applied warped Bayesian linear regression normative models to T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging data ... (see https://github. com/amarquand/PCNtoolkit, version = 0.21)

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The response variable was voxelwise white matter volume (WMV) estimated using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) of T1-weighted anatomical MRI scans via the CAT12 toolbox.
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Segal2025.pdf.md: METHODS AND MATERIALS / Voxel-Scale WMV Heterogeneity; 1-s2.0-S2451902225001272-mmc1.pdf.md: Supplementary Methods / Anatomical data
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: We estimated voxelwise WMV using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) of T1-weighted anatomical MRI scans ... voxel-wise WMV was estimated using the Computational Anatomy Toolbox (CAT12 r113)

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.answer: Age-related: Age; Demographics: Sex; Site/Scanner: Site
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative models predicted WMV as a function of age, sex, and scan site. Age effects were modeled using B-spline basis expansion to capture non-linearities.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.location: Segal2025.pdf.md: METHODS AND MATERIALS / Voxel-Scale WMV Heterogeneity; 1-s2.0-S2451902225001272-mmc1.pdf.md: Supplementary Methods / Normative modelling
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: predict WMV as a function of age, sex, and site ... B-spline basis expansion over age was used to model non-linear effects ... To handle the site effect, we included scan site as a covariate
